text:
[NDLC.2.2] **`settings` must set every capability, and the loader
derives nothing.** Its keys must be exactly the capabilities of
[LCAP.1]: a capability left unset is an error, not a default
(`DS_VALIDATE_DIALECT_INCOMPLETE`), and a key naming no capability is
`DS_VALIDATE_DIALECT_UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY`. The settings must satisfy the
fundamental constraints of [LCAP.3.8]
(`DS_VALIDATE_DIALECT_DEPENDENCY`), and must set `realtime` and
`constspace` `false`, which are deferred in this edition
(`DS_VALIDATE_REALTIME_DEFERRED`, [LCAP.2.1.5]).

Defaulting an unset capability would be the silent behaviour this rule
exists to prevent, and the cost is concrete: when a capability is
**added** to the registry, every existing dialect file would take a value
for it by omission, and compiles would keep succeeding while the tier
silently gained or lost a construct. Requiring every key converts that
into a loud failure when the definition is loaded, which is the point.

alloy.name: ndlc_2_2__accepted
alloy.note: Models the three refusals the clause names first (incomplete, unknown capability, dependency) over any registry. The clause's fourth refusal, a definition setting `realtime` or `constspace` `true` (`DS_VALIDATE_REALTIME_DEFERRED`, [LCAP.2.1.5]), is not modelled: the registry here has no named keys, so the model accepts a definition this edition refuses. The derived checks hold with or without it.
